deep.reconstruction:
This page holds no derivation. It is one sheet of a large hand-drawn table of quadratic-residue characters. It continues the previous sheet (columns 367–503) and the next sheet (columns 661–827).

Layout:
- Rows: the primes 439, 443, 449, 457, 461, 463, 467, 479, 487, 491, 499, 503, 509, 521, and 523 in red.
- Columns: the 24 primes 509, 521, …, 659, written at top and bottom.
- Entries: a small circle at (row p, column q).

Meaning of a circle (my reconstruction, verified below): a circle means q is a quadratic residue mod p, i.e. the Legendre symbol (q/p) = +1. A blank cell means (q/p) = −1.

Direction of the relation. It matters only when p ≡ q ≡ 3 (mod 4), because then reciprocity flips the sign:
- Row 439, column 547: no circle. Here 547 ≡ 108 = 4·27 (mod 439) and (3/439) = −1, so (547/439) = −1. By contrast (439/547) = +1.
- So the relation is 'column is a residue of row', not the reverse.

The red row 523, checked by hand:
- Residues found: 509, 521, 547, 563, 577, 587, 593, 599, 601, 613, 617, 619, 641, 647, 653.
- Sample reductions:
  - 509: (509/523) = (523/509) = (14/509) = (2/509)(7/509) = (−1)(−1) = +1.
  - 547: (547/523) = (24/523) = (2/523)(3/523) = (−1)(−1) = +1.
  - 577: (577/523) = (54/523) = (2/523)(3/523)^3 = +1.
  - 647: (647/523) = (124/523) = (31/523) = +1.
  - 653: (653/523) = (130/523) = (2)(5)(13) = (−1)(−1)(+1) = +1.
- Non-residues, matching the blanks: 541, 557, 569, 571, 607, 631, 643, 659.

Black rows, sample checks:
- Row 439 has circles at 509 and 541. Indeed (70/439) = +1 and (102/439) = +1.
- Row 439 is blank at 521, since (82/439) = −1.

Other features:
- Rows 509 and 521 are essentially unfilled. They carry only a circle on the 'diagonal' (column 509, resp. 521). Row 523 likewise seems to carry a red mark under column 523. These appear to be markers for the table's diagonal or the start of a row, not residue entries.
- The connecting strokes join circles in horizontally or vertically adjacent cells. They form polyomino-like clusters, apparently a visual aid for reading and checking the pattern. They carry no extra arithmetic content.
- The circled '10' is the folio number; the red '19' is a later foliation.

Purpose: this is an extension of the residue tables of the type of Disquisitiones Arithmeticae Table II. Such tables were used empirically for quadratic reciprocity, quadratic forms and class-number work.
errors: No arithmetic errors found in the sampled entries. All red-row entries were checked by hand, and several black-row entries were spot-checked.
The circles at (509,509), (521,521) and (523,523) cannot denote (p/p) = +1, since the symbol is 0 there. They are presumably diagonal or start markers, not residue claims.

results.what: Table of quadratic residue characters (q/p) for primes p in 439..523 and q in 509..659; a circle means q is a quadratic residue mod p.
results.modern_name: Table of Legendre symbols / quadratic residue table
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (Disquisitiones Arithmeticae 1801, Table II), with later extensions by Jacobi (Canon arithmeticus 1839) and others

results.what: Graphical joining of adjacent residue marks by lines, so the pattern reads as clusters.
results.modern_name: Visual/pattern representation of a residue matrix

deep.surprise_reason: Gauss's extensive residue tables are well known, and Table II of the Disquisitiones is of exactly this kind. This sheet is a routine computational extension. The only mildly curious features are the connect-the-adjacent-circles style and the diagonal markers.
